methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 298 consecutive HCC liver transplant recipients spanning 2000-2022 with median 64-month follow-up, yielding 56 recurrences and 119 deaths, providing reasonable event counts for survival modeling. Appropriate analytical approach including Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, Cox multivariable regression, and importantly competing-risks analysis (cumulative incidence function) to account for non-recurrence deaths. RETREAT score calculation follows the original definition and uses a cohort-adapted cutoff (>=4) justified by score distribution. Limitations include single-center, Italian-only cohort, evolving listing criteria over 22 years not formally stratified in sensitivity analyses (authors acknowledge underpowered era-specific analyses), and retrospective dichotomous MVI without contemporary refined grading. Methods section is truncated in one place ('Patients were excluded from this study in case of' followed by nothing), indicating a minor reporting error.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort (Oxford 2b) that validates a widely adopted post-transplant HCC recurrence prediction score (RETREAT) in a contemporary European real-world setting spanning an era of expanding LT eligibility (Milan to Up-to-Seven criteria, down-staging). Findings directly support post-LT surveillance intensity, immunosuppression tailoring, and identification of candidates for potential adjuvant strategies. Clinically useful external validation, though not practice-changing because RETREAT is already established.

reporting_quality.justification: As an external validation of a prediction model, TRIPOD applies; the paper reports setting, participants, eligibility criteria evolution, predictors (RETREAT components), outcomes, and performance via Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses. However, TRIPOD is not explicitly cited, no calibration metrics (Brier score, calibration plots) or discrimination statistics (C-index, AUC) are reported against the original RETREAT publication as would be standard for external validation, only categorical HR comparisons. The exclusion-criteria sentence is incomplete in methods, indicating editorial oversight. IRB approval and consent are reported. No data or code sharing.

novelty_literature.justification: RETREAT score has been externally validated in multiple prior cohorts (van Hooff 2022, Pommergaard 2019, Mehta 2018 UNOS, Reddy 2022 UK) as explicitly cited. This study adds an Italian single-center validation over 22 years, with the incremental contributions of: (a) competing-risks analysis, (b) longer follow-up (up to 15 years), and (c) testing a RETREAT+ modification adding tumor grade (which did not improve performance). These are minor incremental contributions to a well-established validation literature rather than novel methodology.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly written with logical structure, clinically grounded rationale, and an appropriately extensive discussion comparing findings to prior validation studies and positioning the score within evolving transplant oncology practice. Figures and tables are clearly referenced, and limitations are thoughtfully addressed including MVI grading and era heterogeneity. Minor issues include the incomplete methods sentence about exclusions and some repetitive sentences in the discussion on RETREAT's generalizability. Overall publication-quality.

key_strengths: Large (n=298) single-center consecutive cohort with extended follow-up (median 64 months, up to 15 years) and 56 recurrences providing adequate event counts
Formal competing-risks analysis accounting for non-HCC mortality, with RETREAT retaining independent association (HR 2.3 medium-risk, 6.4 high-risk)
Cohort spans evolving eligibility criteria (Milan to Up-to-Seven, increasing down-staging) providing real-world heterogeneity
Appropriate supplementary analyses including 5-year-specific Cox model and RETREAT+ (adding tumor grade) showing no additional benefit, supporting score parsimony
Explicit acknowledgment of inability to apply RETREAT pre-LT due to explant-dependent variables and limitations of dichotomous MVI grading
key_concerns: Single-center Italian cohort over 22 years with evolving protocols; era-specific sensitivity analyses were not performed due to power constraints
Incomplete exclusion-criteria sentence in methods suggests editorial oversight and obscures cohort selection transparency
No formal calibration (calibration plot, Brier score) or discrimination (C-index) metrics reported as expected for TRIPOD-compliant external validation; only categorical HRs
TRIPOD not explicitly referenced; no data or code sharing
Incremental contribution over multiple prior external validations (van Hooff, Pommergaard, Mehta, Reddy); primary novelty is the competing-risks framing and long follow-up
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent real-world validation of the RETREAT score with competing-risks analysis and long follow-up, suitable for a Tier 3 oncology or hepatology journal with minor revisions to complete methodological reporting, add formal calibration/discrimination metrics, and fix the incomplete exclusion-criteria sentence.
